Repertoire includes selections from standard operatic literature as well as scenes from works spanning diverse styles and periods. Open to qualified singers by audition, Opera Theater culminates in public performances that integrate the elements of music, theater, and stagecraft.

By writing original compositions for various instrumentations, students gain skills in the artistic use of pitch, rhythm, melody, timbre and harmony. 20th and 21st century styles and techniques are utilized, and students acquire skill in music improvisation. Students gain competency in the basics of music notation utilizing both calligraphy and composition software.
courses.title: Class Composition I

courses.description: Students develop further music composition skill by exploring techniques necessary for coherent creative expression. By writing original compositions for various instrumentations, students gain abilities in the artistic use of pitch, rhythm, melody, timbre and harmony. 20th and 21st century styles and techniques are utilized. Students gain technology competency in the use of composition software and by learning the basics of digital audio and video editing of recorded performances.
courses.title: Class Composition II

courses.description: A study of tonal, common-practice music in the Western art music tradition from the perspective of Schenkerian (reductive) analysis. Activities include investigations of harmony, voice leading, form, and implications for performance. Encourages students to debate the merits of different analyzes of the same work. Culminates in scholarly research by the student that builds upon previous Schenkerian analyzes. A writing-intensive course.
courses.title: Introduction to Schenker

courses.description: Analysis and principles of writing in the contrapuntal styles of the common practice period to the present.
courses.title: Counterpoint

courses.description: This course surveys 20th- and 21st-century musical styles and theoretical systems, teaching students how to analyze a variety of works in which Common-Practice Period norms of tonality, rhythm, form, timbre, and texture have been superseded by new developments. Corresponding compositional exercises deepen student understanding of these new approaches. Topics include free atonality, serialism, neoclassicism, minimalism, allusions, chance, and electronic composition. The course prepares students to analyze music, write model compositions, and develop analytical papers.
courses.title: Contemporary Analytical and Compositional Techniques

Students team-teach lessons in undergraduate courses in the School of Music and prepare materials for potential graduate school applications.

Students fulfill projects that synthesize and disseminate their work through a lecture, lecture-performance, or scholarly paper.

Students fulfill projects that synthesize and disseminate their work through a culminating lecture-performance.

courses.description: This course provides an overview of the music therapy field, introducing students to its history, scope of practice, clinical applications, and professional competencies. In this course, students will explore how music therapy integrates musical, psychological, and therapeutic principles to address the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of individuals across diverse populations and settings.
courses.title: Introduction to the Profession of Music Therapy

courses.description: This course provides an introduction to foundational principles of music therapy practice. Students examine professional ethics and competencies while developing beginning clinical skills through case studies and guided observation. This course provides the foundation for practicum and advanced clinical training in music therapy.
courses.title: Clinical Foundations in Music Therapy

courses.description: This course introduces theories, principles, and methods of music therapy practice. Students explore the therapeutic relationship, clinical applications of music across populations, and the integration of psychological and physiological concepts into treatment planning. Emphasis is placed on historical and contemporary models of music therapy, ethical standards of practice, and developing observation, assessment, and intervention skills.
courses.title: Music Therapy Theory & Application I

courses.description: This course develops functional guitar skills essential for the practice of music therapy. Students will learn chord vocabulary, strumming and fingerpicking patterns, transposition, improvisation, and song-leading techniques that support therapeutic goals in clinical settings.
courses.title: Guitar Skills for Music Therapists

courses.description: This course is a supervised clinical experience introducing students to the application of music therapy in professional settings. Students observe, assist, and begin to facilitate music experiences with diverse populations under the guidance of board-certified music therapists. Emphasis is placed on developing professional skills, including session planning, clinical observation, therapeutic presence, ethical practice, and reflective journaling. Practicum I provides students with a structured opportunity to connect classroom learning with clinical practice, laying the foundation for progressive practicum experiences and professional competency in music therapy.
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum I

courses.description: This course provides continued supervised clinical training for students in music therapy, building upon skills developed in Practicum I. Students engage in structured field experiences in healthcare, educational, and/or community settings, applying music therapy methods with increasing independence and clinical responsibility. Emphasis is placed on treatment planning, implementation, observation, documentation, and reflection. Students will further develop therapeutic presence, adaptability, and professional communication skills while working with diverse client populations.
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum II

courses.description: This course introduces students to the principles, methods, and applications of research and assessment in music therapy. Students will explore qualitative and quantitative research designs, evidence-based practices, and ethical considerations in clinical work. Emphasis is placed on analyzing scholarly literature and applying research findings to clinical practice. Students will also gain hands-on experience with assessment tools and techniques used to evaluate client needs, track progress, and measure treatment outcomes.
courses.title: Music Therapy Research & Assessment

courses.description: This course provides music therapy students with expanded clinical experience and increasing responsibility in a supervised setting. Students engage in structured music therapy sessions across diverse populations, with emphasis on session planning, treatment documentation, therapeutic communication, and professional ethics. Building on prior practica, students are expected to demonstrate greater independence in leading interventions, integrating music therapy methods with clinical goals, and applying theoretical knowledge to practice. Regular supervision and reflective assignments guide students in refining their clinical musicianship, interpersonal skills, and professional identity as developing music therapists.
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum III

courses.description: This course builds upon the foundations established in Music Therapy Theory & Application I, advancing students’ understanding of clinical techniques, treatment planning, and theoretical models in music therapy. Emphasis is placed on the application of music interventions for diverse populations, including individuals across the lifespan with varying developmental, medical, and psychological needs.
courses.title: Music Therapy Theory & Application II

courses.description: This advanced practicum provides supervised clinical experience in diverse music therapy settings, emphasizing greater independence, leadership, and professional competence. Students refine their ability to assess client needs, design and implement individualized interventions, and evaluate outcomes using evidence-based practices. The course integrates advanced clinical musicianship with professional documentation, treatment planning, and ethical decision-making. By the fourth practicum, students are expected to demonstrate increased autonomy in leading sessions, collaborate effectively with interdisciplinary teams, and begin developing a personal therapeutic style that reflects best practices in the field. Regular supervision and peer feedback guide the integration of theory, research, and practice, preparing students for the culminating internship and entry into professional music therapy practice.
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum IV

courses.description: This course advances students’ understanding of the theoretical foundations and applied practices of music therapy with a focus on clinical decision-making and treatment planning across diverse populations. Students refine skills in assessment, goal development, intervention design, and documentation while integrating current research and evidence-based practices. Emphasis is placed on the therapeutic relationship, clinical improvisation, and ethical considerations in music therapy practice. Through lecture, discussion, and applied experiences, students deepen their capacity to synthesize theory and application in preparation for advanced practicum and clinical work.
courses.title: Music Therapy Theory & Application III

courses.description: This course is the culminating practicum providing music therapy majors with advanced, supervised clinical training in preparation for internship. Students refine their clinical musicianship, therapeutic presence, and professional competencies through immersive placements in diverse healthcare and community settings. Emphasis is placed on independent treatment planning, implementation, documentation, and evaluation, as well as integration of theoretical knowledge with clinical decision-making. Students are expected to demonstrate entry-level proficiency in applying music therapy methods across populations, collaborating with interdisciplinary teams, and adhering to professional and ethical standards. Successful completion of this practicum confirms readiness for internship and transition into the professional field of music therapy.
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum V

courses.description: A broad survey of the major topics in psychology including, but not limited to, research methodology, biological and social factors influencing behavior, development, learning, memory, personality, and abnormal.
courses.title: Introduction to General Psychology

courses.description: This class introduces students to human development, from conception to death, emphasizing biological, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development. Scientific approaches for studying developmental psychology stress the importance of research methodology and research findings across the life-span. Theories of development and applications to real-world problems provide a context for understanding how humans change during the life-cycle.
courses.title: Introduction to Human Development
